questions.problem:
$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x\in [-\pi ,0] \\ 1, & x\in (0,\pi )\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the function $F(x)$ shown above. Find the value to which the Fourier series of the $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ converges when $x=\pi .$

The Fourier series converges to {{field-1}} when $x=\pi .$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is a $2L$-periodic piecewise smooth function with the corresponding Fourier series

$$
S(x)=\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x).
$$

Then, the series converges for all $x\in R.$

- If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x,$ then the series converges to the value of the function at this point:

$$
S(x)=f(x)
$$

- If $f(x)$ has a jump discontinuity at $x,$ then the series converges to the midpoint between the values of left- and right-sided limits of the function at this point:

$$
S(x)=\frac{{f}^{-}(x)+{f}^{+}(x)}{2}
$$

where ${f}^{-}(x)$ and ${f}^{-}(x)$ are the left- and right-sided limits of the function at this point, respectively.

Notice that the $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of our function $F(x)$ is not continuous at $x=\pi .$ The one-sided limits at this point are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-}(\pi ) & ={lim}_{x\to {\pi }^{-}}f(x)=1 \\ {f}^{+}(\pi ) & ={lim}_{x\to {\pi }^{+}}f(x)=0\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ converges to 

$$
\frac{{f}^{-}(\pi )+{f}^{+}(\pi )}{2}=\frac{1+0}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
$$

questions.problem:
$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-1, & x\in [-4,0] \\ 3, & x\in (0,4)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the function $F(x)$ shown above. The Fourier series of the $8$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{8}{\pi (2n-1)}sin\,(\frac{(2n-1)\pi x}{4}).
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below.

At $x=-2,$ we have

$$
sin\,(\frac{(2n-1)\pi \cdot (-2)}{4})={{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is 
{{field-2}}
at $x=-2,$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(-2)={{field-3}}.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{2n-1}={{field-4}}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼1+\frac{8}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot sin\,(\frac{(2n-1)\pi x}{4}).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=-2,$ we have

$$
sin\,(\frac{(2n-1)\pi \cdot (-2)}{4})=sin\,(\frac{\pi }{2}-n\pi )=(-1)^{n}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=-2,$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(-2)=-1.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-2) & =1+\frac{8}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot sin\,(\frac{(2n-1)\pi \cdot (-2)}{4}) \\ -1 & =1+\frac{8}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot (-1)^{n} \\ -2 & =\frac{8}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{2n-1} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n}}{2n-1} & =-\frac{\pi }{4} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{2n-1} & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-3, & x\in [-\pi ,0] \\ 1, & x\in (0,\pi )\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the function $F(x)$ shown above. The Fourier series of the $2\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is given by

$$
f(x)∼-1+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{8}{\pi (2n-1)}sin\,((2n-1)x).
$$

Select the correct options in the reasoning below.

At $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we have

$$
sin\,((2n-1)\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})={{field-1}}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is 
{{field-2}}
at $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(\frac{\pi }{2})={{field-3}}.
$$

Therefore, we have 

$$
{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{2n-1}={{field-4}}.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we rewrite our Fourier series as

$$
f(x)∼-1+\frac{8}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot sin\,((2n-1)x).
$$

Now, notice that at $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ we have

$$
sin\,((2n-1)\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})=sin\,(-\frac{\pi }{2}+n\pi )=(-1)^{n+1}.
$$

Since $f(x)$ is $\text{continuous}$ at $x=\frac{\pi }{2},$ the corresponding Fourier series converges to 

$$
f(\frac{\pi }{2})=1.
$$

 

Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-1+\frac{8}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot sin\,((2n-1)\cdot \frac{\pi }{2}) \\ 1 & =-1+\frac{8}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{1}{2n-1}\cdot (-1)^{n+1} \\ 2 & =\frac{8}{\pi }{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{2n-1} \\ {\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }\frac{(-1)^{n+1}}{2n-1} & =\frac{\pi }{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-4, & x\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},0) \\ 2\operatorname{sin}⁡x, & x\in [0,\frac{\pi }{2})\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the function $F(x)$ shown above. Find the value to which the Fourier series of the $\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ converges when $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$

The Fourier series converges to {{field-1}} when $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Suppose that $f(x)$ is a $2L$-periodic piecewise smooth function with the corresponding Fourier series

$$
S(x)=\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{L}x).
$$

Then, the series converges for all $x\in R.$

- If $f(x)$ is continuous at $x,$ then the series converges to the value of the function at this point:

$$
S(x)=f(x)
$$

- If $f(x)$ has a jump discontinuity at $x,$ then the series converges to the midpoint between the values of left- and right-sided limits of the function at this point:

$$
S(x)=\frac{{f}^{-}(x)+{f}^{+}(x)}{2}
$$

where ${f}^{-}(x)$ and ${f}^{+}(x)$ are the left- and right-sided limits of the function at this point, respectively.

Notice that the $\pi $-periodic extension $f(x)$ of our function $F(x)$ is not continuous at $x=\frac{\pi }{2}.$ The one-sided limits at this point are the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-}\,(\frac{\pi }{2}) & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{-}}f(x)=2\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})=2 \\ {f}^{+}\,(\frac{\pi }{2}) & ={lim}_{x\to (\pi /2)^{+}}f(x)=-4\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the Fourier series of $f(x)$ converges to 

$$
\frac{{f}^{-}\,(\frac{\pi }{2})+{f}^{+}\,(\frac{\pi }{2})}{2}=\frac{2+(-4)}{2}=-1.
$$
